note: This package pins almost nothing of its own, and that is deliberate. What a header means is pinned in snes-rom-image-python against Nintendo's development manual, and where a header sits is pinned in snes-mapper-python. Copying either here would create a second source of truth that will drift. What is left is the two facts that belong to this correction and to no sibling.

order: snes-rom-image-python and snes-mapper-python, for anything about a header
the image itself, confirmed by digest at both ends of the correction
authority.why: The correction is small and somebody else's packages do all of it. What is left here is checking at both ends, which is what makes it safe to run unattended: an image is confirmed against four digests before anything touches it, and the result is confirmed against four more before it is written.

comparedAgainst.what: Real images at every link of both chains, each confirmed against four digests before and after the correction.

developmentManual.title: SNES Development Manual, Book 1
developmentManual.note: Not read here. The size byte this correction writes follows a rule the manual implies rather than a row it prints, and snes-rom-image-python is where that rule is derived, pinned and checked against retail cartridges. Naming the sibling keeps the reading in one place; repeating the digest lets a reader confirm they hold the same scan without opening the other repository.

documentsNote: One entry, reached through a sibling. This repository reads no document of its own: it corrects twelve bytes per image and every claim about what those bytes mean belongs to a member below it.

imageBytes.why: Ninety six megabit, which is what the decompressed game occupies.
imageBytes.evidence: The images themselves. Every edition in the manifest is exactly this length, and one that is not is refused before anything reads it.

sizeByte.why: What the header must declare for an image of that length.
sizeByte.evidence: Nintendo's rule, pinned in snes-rom-image-python: the size byte is the base two logarithm of the length in kilobytes, rounded up. 12288 KB gives 14.
sizeByte.note: Nintendo's table stops at 64 megabit, so this figure comes from the rule rather than from a printed row. The rule reproduces every row the manual does print, and a table of five rows cannot be the whole answer because cartridges below its smallest row exist and carry a size byte.

notStated: Anything about the S-DD1. This package corrects a header on an image somebody else already decompressed; it does not decompress anything. That chip is snes-sdd1-python.
Anything about hardware behaviour at all. This reads a file, rewrites six bytes in each of its two header mirrors, and writes it back.
Whether the decompression that produced the input is correct. The input is taken as given and confirmed only to be the file the manifest names.
